name: encrypted-value-unknown-entity-tolerated
description: a REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE naming an entity the consumer does not know must not fail the run; the spec lets a consumer drop it, so delivery is deliberately not required
kill: make an unresolvable entityId fatal in the reducer, or materialise a message for it — the spec permits DROPPING the event (MAY), so this fixture must not require delivery: it pins tolerance and the conversation staying intact, nothing more

dotnet.intentional: The tolerance the fixture requires holds — the run completes and the conversation survives — but .NET materialises the encrypted value as its own reasoning-content update keyed on the entityId, so an unknown entity leaves an extra contentless message behind instead of being stored nowhere. That extra message IS the whole divergence, and the messageCount and messages below are what pin it: this lane must end up with the answer plus one empty message carrying the unresolvable id, rather than with the answer alone. Neither this override nor the base expectation states an event list, deliberately. The specification lets a consumer DROP a REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE whose entity it cannot resolve, so no lane may be held to delivering it, and naming the events either client happens to hand its application would freeze one implementation's surface into a requirement the spec does not make.
